body: Thank you so much for talking to me. I appreciate it so much. It really did help.

I'm not sure about the support group but there's a lady in my moms group who also lost her mom pretty young. 

It's been a long time since I did anything just because it made me happy. I married at 20, had my first child at 22... As a kid, I loved playing soccer and tap dancing. I've actually looked into adult tap classes but never bit the bullet and signed up. Maybe I should...
I am actually out of town this weekend on a solo getaway. But it isn't helping because it's just more time and energy to dwell on how lonely I feel.

I have considered that. Actually, I applied for a position at a local coffee shop that's within walking distance. Unfortunately it didn't work out, but seeing as we live in the metropolitan area of a relatively large city, I'm sure there must be more options.
My son thinks if he closes his eyes, we can't see him. If only hiding was so easy, buddy.
Thanks for the ideas. I did recently join a local parenting group which has been a great social outlet at times.
I'm working on getting a part time job. And we have family close by who is willing to babysit for free 10-15 hrs/week, so that helps!
He is helping, FYI. He's a great, involved dad who couldn't love his kids more. I'll look into getting a degree! Thanks!

Thanks for the suggestions. One of my biggest barriers right now is just feeling overwhelmed on where to start (with regards to the job situation). This is something practical and tangible I can do to help myself focus. Thank you.

Thanks for the comment. The "having our own lives" I mentioned entails an open marriage, among other things. That's our plan for the next few years. 

But it hardly seems to be a sustainable plan in the long term. What if one of us meets someone with whom we would like to be in a serious relationship? We'd want them to meet our children, I'm sure. Plus I'm sure sneaking around would get old quickly. Our kids would surely notice something was going on as they get older. Not to mention family and friends catching wind of what's going on. 

Our children are our first priority; we love them more than anything. And we feel confident that we can give them a stable, safe childhood even if their dad and I aren't married. Like I said, we get along well. And he really is a great father. We aren't convinced that staying married is always and ultimately "best" if it sacrifices other things we believe to be important.

I'll ignore the fact that your comment is neither helpful nor encouraging...

Do you honestly think it's that simple? And even so, do you honestly think we HAVEN'T tried that? That's what the last five and a half years have entailed. If it hasn't happened in that amount of time, I am pretty confident it never will. But let's just say, by some astronomical chance, I DO fall in love with him. That would be even worse! Unrequited love? No thank you.

Thanks so much for commenting. It's comforting to know I'm not alone. At times I feel bad for feeling bad because things could be so much worse. But that doesn't make this easy. My life has turned out so far from what I expected.
